Yes— our country missed the chance to fix Social Security decades ago. Congress was too scared to make hard decisions. Still is.

When our generation retires without a safety net, everyone is to blame. Politicians are too afraid to have difficult and truthful conversations about Social Security reform because their voters won’t let them.

posts.text:
And last year, Congress made the problem worse by scrapping rules that prevented some workers from collecting both a public pension and full Social Security benefits (that they DID NOT pay in to).

I voted No.

Because it’s not worth paying off a small constituency for their vote while sacrificing an entire generation’s safety net guarantee.

But that’s what the politics demanded anyway.

posts.text:
Solutions are easy in theory, but controversial in practice. Americans need to have rational conversations about ideas like raising the retirement age, reigning in COLA increases, means-tested benefits, and privatizing what we can so that we can all take advantage of market returns.

But we won’t. Not until the system collapses in the 2030’s.

Social Security was never designed to be anyone’s retirement plan. It’s a safety net. And my generation is gonna get screwed out of it.

The media wants you to believe Border Patrol is dropping a massive steel wall through Big Bend National Park. Not true.

Inside the park, there’s a 17 mile stretch of vehicle barriers, patrol roads, cameras, and sensors. No walls. No “destroying Big Bend.” No outrage necessary. Just stopping illegal crossings of our border, like we should.
